core: auth.AttemptLimiter: keys wait after 5 counted attempts in 300 s: 60 s, doubling per new wait to 900 s. During a wait the request is refused before the password is checked and does not lengthen the wait. A key quiet for 900 s after its last wait or attempt is forgotten; at most 4096 keys, stalest dropped first; memory only.

Core.login(client=): one count per account (user id when the user exists, so user name and e-mail share it; otherwise the typed name) and one per client address. Failure (wrong password, unknown user or inactive account) counts on both. Success clears the account; the address is cleared too unless it also counted attempts on other accounts, then only this account's failures are forgotten.
Core.register(client=): every sign-up request counts per client address, accepted or refused, same waits.
New diagnostic AUTH-RATE-LIMITED (429, effect none, params retry_after_s) with Retry-After header.
api.Admission: 16 request slots plus 4 reserved for runner routes and job cancel; 5 s wait, then 503 CORE-BUSY (effect none, retry safe, Retry-After 2). The change feed (long wait) takes no slot.

_TlsServer: at most 64 connections being served and 16 per client address; extra ones are closed at accept, before TLS, without a thread. Timeout per connection 30 s (handshake, idle keep-alive, read/write).

TLS close: after the handshake the TLS socket owns the connection; the server now shuts it down and closes it when the handler ends (finished or interrupted). Before, only the detached plain socket was 'closed' and the TLS socket was left to the garbage collector (the ResourceWarning).

db.Database: max_open 32 connections in use (the 8-connection idle cache is not a limit), 5 s wait, then PoolBusy -> 503 CORE-STORAGE-UNAVAILABLE (reason PoolBusy, effect unknown as before). A nested transaction on the same thread does not wait for a second place.
Login now validates password type (a non-string no longer reaches scrypt) and splits the lookup and session insert into two short transactions.
tests: tests/core/test_limits.py (new, 17): limiter policy with a test clock; through HTTPS: refusal and recovery, user name and e-mail sharing a count, one address failing on many accounts, no permanent lock after the longest wait, sign-up per address, restart clears; busy refusal with Runner heartbeat and cancel passing on reserved slots and the change feed without a slot; database cap without self-deadlock and its API diagnostic; connection caps; TLS sockets closed after completed, interrupted, handshake-never-sent, non-TLS and immediately closed connections (no server-side ResourceWarning).

limitations: No independent review yet; no installed proof (S4).

Anyone on the LAN who knows a user name can make that account wait (up to 15 min per wait, renewable by failing again); it is never permanent and needs no administrator to clear. Counting per account and address pair instead would remove this at the cost of the per-account protection; not changed without a user decision.
Users on the Core's own computer share the address 127.0.0.1 for the per-address count.
Limits live in memory: a Core restart clears them (decided).

The connection cap is reached before the request is known, so the Runner margin exists at request level only; a client holding 16 idle connections per address from 4 or more addresses could fill the 64 connections for up to 30 s each.
The numbers (64, 16, 16+4, 32, 5 s, 30 s) are sized for a small LAN team and were not measured under real load (no load test against the real install, per the work order).
Dependency inventory only; no advisory scan.
